split/copies: To train on several GPUs at once, give each one a full copy of the weights, w.
split/slice: Every step, split the batch into slices, one per GPU. Four GPUs with thirty two examples each make a batch of a hundred and twenty eight.
split/grad: Each GPU computes the gradient on its own slice: the average over its own thirty two examples, all four at the same time.
average/per: For one weight, the four GPUs might find gradients of two, minus one, three and zero.
average/mean: They send them to each other and average: four over four, one. With equal slices, that is exactly the gradient of the whole batch of a hundred and twenty eight.
average/step: Every GPU then takes the same step, with the same gradient, so the copies stay identical.
average/send: So each step, what travels between the GPUs is gradients: one number per parameter, from every GPU. The examples stay where they are.
epoch/epoch: An epoch is still one pass through all N examples, and each step uses one whole batch, across all the GPUs.
epoch/steps: So an epoch takes N over B steps. Twelve thousand eight hundred examples, in batches of a hundred and twenty eight: a hundred steps.
epoch/more: With eight GPUs at thirty two each, the batch is two hundred and fifty six: fifty steps, each covering twice the data.
